thesis: PTC rose about 34% after Schneider Electric announced a definitive all-cash agreement at $205/share (~$22.6B, ~42% premium to the $144.03 prior close). This suggests the move is a takeout re-rating, so remaining upside is likely limited to the deal spread. Strongest counter-evidence: close is not expected until about Q3 2027 and needs HSR, CFIUS and a PTC shareholder vote, so deal-break and timing risk exist, which lowers the appeal of a directional long. No litigation, restatement, offering or going-concern issue found (search-level only).
invalidation: A deal break or competing bid would change the read.

thesis: RXO rose about 23% after C.H. Robinson agreed to acquire it for $17.25 cash plus 0.0856 CHRW shares per share (implied ~$30.25, ~29% premium to the 10/2 close), close targeted 1H 2027. This suggests the move reflects deal pricing, with part of the consideration tied to CHRW's share price. Strongest counter-evidence: closing needs regulatory clearance and an RXO vote and the cash is debt-financed, so completion risk exists and upside above the offer looks limited; this does not support a directional long. No active litigation with a near-term deadline, restatement, offering or turnover issue found.
invalidation: A deal break or higher competing bid would change the read.

thesis: The heavy volume on 10/5 likely reflects index-inclusion demand ahead of Twilio's S&P 500 add effective 10/6, after a ~52% 60-day run. This suggests much of the move is mechanical buying that may fade once inclusion completes. Strongest counter-evidence: HSBC downgraded to Reduce on 9/25 on valuation (an opinion, not a company disclosure). No new raise, litigation deadline, restatement or turnover issue found. Q3 earnings expected around 10/29.
invalidation: A fundamental company-disclosed catalyst beyond index flows would change the read.

thesis: FormFactor's 11x volume on a -1% day fits S&P index reconstitution trading rather than a new disclosure; the 60-day gain is supported by Q2 results (revenue $258.2M, +31.9% y/y; EPS $0.82 vs ~$0.59 expected) and a Deutsche Bank Buy initiation on 9/30. Strongest counter-evidence: index-driven volume can reverse after the effective date and the stock is already extended after a strong run, which tempers but does not negate the fundamental read. Technoprobe v. FormFactor is on file but no ruling date within 90 days was verified. Next binary: Q3 earnings 10/27.
invalidation: A post-index selloff below recent support or a Q3 miss would change the read.

thesis: SPCX rose 7.6% on bullish Morgan Stanley commentary and reports of a potential exclusive TSMC deal, following launch milestones. This suggests the move is partly sentiment and rumor, with the TSMC element unconfirmed. Strongest counter-evidence: a further tranche of the IPO lockup unlocks after Q3 earnings and remaining restrictions lift around 12/8, a supply overhang. Recent IPO with elevated volatility; search depth on legal/governance was shallow.
invalidation: Confirmation of the TSMC deal with disclosed terms would change the read.

thesis: AMD's latest disclosed news is the Sept 28 all-stock ~$8.2B agreement to acquire World Labs (close expected by end-2026), but the broader ~30% rally appears to ride sector-wide AI-chip demand rather than a company-specific confirmed event. Strongest counter-evidence is valuation and share issuance for the deal; the issuance is small relative to a ~$1T cap and is not an offering/ATM. No scheduled litigation ruling, restatement or operational C-suite exit found. This suggests a momentum/sector-driven read with pullback sensitivity.
invalidation: A sector-wide AI-chip selloff or deal complications would change the read.

thesis: Dell's fiscal Q2 report raised FY2027 AI-server revenue guidance from $60B to $74B and total revenue to about $192B at midpoint, with record AI orders ($60.9B) and ~$95B backlog; this is a company-disclosed catalyst. Strongest counter-evidence: management named memory-chip supply as the main constraint on converting backlog; this suggests a timing rather than demand issue and does not change the read materially given disclosed orders. No scheduled litigation ruling (the $1B class settlement was resolved in 2022), restatement, offering or operational executive exit found. No binary catalyst identified in the next ~2 weeks.
invalidation: Order cancellations, guidance cut, or a prolonged memory-supply shortfall would change the read.

thesis: Intel's early-October jump was attributed by press to a sector/narrative catalyst (agentic-AI CPU expectations) rather than a new company disclosure, and shares fell 10/5 on profit-taking and reports TSMC could join Musk's Terafab project. Strongest counter-evidence: Q2 data-center/AI revenue rose 59% y/y and the CEO said it can fill only about half of CPU demand. Offsets: a Delaware derivative suit over the US government stock deal, VLSI and EC accruals, and estimated Q3 laptop share loss. No scheduled ruling in the next 90 days verified. Evidence reads as mixed.
invalidation: A company-disclosed supply/demand catalyst or share stabilization would change the read.

thesis: Micron reported record fiscal Q4 (Sept 30): adjusted EPS $33.42 vs $31.61 expected, revenue $54.23B vs $51.07B, with FQ1 guidance of ~$61.5B revenue, driven by AI memory demand; this is confirmed and disclosed alongside a sector-wide memory tailwind. Counter-evidence: a muted post-earnings reaction on cycle worries and a June 2026 N.D. Cal. antitrust class action alleging DRAM supply restriction; no scheduled ruling or trial in the next 90 days was found, so this suggests headline risk. No restatement, offering or operational C-suite exit found. Multiple factors are listed without one clearly dominant.
invalidation: A dispositive ruling, guidance cut, or memory pricing reversal would change the read.

thesis: Marvell holds an Investor Day on Oct 6, with coverage pointing to a ~$18B fiscal 2028 revenue target and growing custom-silicon ties; this suggests the AI-infrastructure thesis is intact. Strongest counter-evidence: the CFO change (resigned effective Jun 15, replaced by a board member) is outside the 90-day window and not tied to operational problems, so it does not change the read; the stock is up ~29% in 60 days so Investor Day expectations may be priced in. The catalyst is pending and could reverse the read. No scheduled litigation, restatement or raise found.
invalidation: A disappointing Investor Day or lowered targets would change the read.

thesis: Nvidia's board authorized an additional $150B of buybacks (remaining $235B) and hyperscaler capex estimates suggest continued demand; the stock is testing all-time highs. Strongest counter-evidence is legal/regulatory: a 2018 securities class action certified Mar 2026, a China SAMR preliminary antitrust finding (Sep 2025) and restricted H200 China sales. No ruling or hearing date within ~90 days was found, so this suggests background risk that does not change the read. The catalyst mixes a company-disclosed buyback with sector-wide AI capex.
invalidation: A scheduled adverse ruling, China restrictions widening, or a capex pullback would change the read.

thesis: AXT reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $47.6M, a return to profit, 45% non-GAAP gross margin and ~$748.8M cash; this suggests AI data-center optics demand is driving results. Strongest counter-evidence: a ~$550M equity offering closed Apr 22 (outside the 90-day window), plus high volatility and reliance on China-based production and PRC export permits; the large cash balance argues against a liquidity concern. Q3 earnings Oct 29 is outside the next ~2 weeks. No pending lawsuit, restatement or C-suite departure found.
invalidation: Loss of PRC export permits, a new equity raise, or a demand slowdown would change the read.

thesis: SK hynix listed ADRs on Nasdaq (priced $149, ~$26.5B raised, 7x oversubscribed) and is a leading HBM supplier; a union dispute was settled in mid-September. This suggests AI memory demand is the driver. Strongest counter-evidence: the offering used ~17.79M newly issued shares, and the exact listing date could not be confirmed, so it may fall inside the ~90-day window and is flagged as dilution risk. The catalyst mixes company events with sector-wide HBM demand. No restatement, scheduled litigation or executive departure found.
invalidation: A weakening of HBM demand or further share overhang would change the read.

thesis: A San Diego federal jury awarded Taction Technology ~$5.7B on Sep 25-26 over haptic patents (infringement found, not willful; Apple says it will appeal), and the stock fell ~2.7% after. This suggests a modest headwind that is small relative to Apple's size, alongside rising memory costs. Near-term catalysts are a reportedly planned Oct 13 event (rumored, not company-confirmed) and Oct 29 earnings. Post-trial motion and appeal timing are not confirmed. No restatement, raise or executive departure found.
invalidation: A larger adverse legal outcome or sustained margin pressure from memory costs would change the read.
